extracted.intended_audience: general readers and media professionals seeking information on the Peabody Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the Peabody Awards' purpose, what kinds of productions are eligible, the submission timeframe, and how winners are selected by the Peabody Board and its committees. Useful for understanding award criteria and process for electronic media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — outstanding public service and achievement in electronic media
rubrics_metrics.description: Peabody Awards are given in recognition of outstanding public service and achievement in electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are organizations and individuals involved in the production or distribution of content for radio, broadcast and cable television, and the Internet. The awards are held in high esteem within the media industry because of their academic affiliation and reputation for discernment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — electronically distributed productions
rubrics_metrics.description: Most electronically distributed productions are eligible for Peabody consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly notes one notable exception: motion pictures intended for theatrical release are not eligible. Awards for Web sites were introduced in 2003; television awards began in 1948.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe — previous calendar year
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions consist of content aired or otherwise distributed during the previous calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each year the Peabody Board collects submissions of content from the prior calendar year for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection body — Peabody Board composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are determined by the Peabody Board, described as a select panel of scholars, critics, and media professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's deliberations are guided by recommendations of special committees whose members are drawn from the University of Georgia community. The board determines the various winners and the awards are presented in the spring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards — unfixed annual total
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific number of Peabody Awards given each year is not fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By the early 21st century, at least 30 awards were bestowed in a typical year, with honorees ranging from television documentaries and prime-time entertainment series to radio news segments and online videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of recognition — programs, projects, bodies of work, and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Peabody Awards may recognize individual programs or projects, an entire body of work by a person, or the work of an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives examples such as Oprah Winfrey (entire body of work) and BBC Radio (institutional recognition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic eligibility — non-American productions allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-American productions are eligible for Peabody Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although non-American productions can be honored, historically they have represented a minority of recipients.
